disclaimer: Controls are inspired by the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark and AWS security best practices. This catalog is not a CIS-certified implementation and does not cover the full benchmark.

controls.title: All enabled regions in the account were audited
controls.rationale: Resources in regions that were not audited are unassessed; attackers favour unmonitored regions.
evidence_requirements: ec2:DescribeRegions enabled regions compared with audited regions
controls.remediation: Re-run the audit with --regions all, or document why specific regions are out of scope.

controls.title: EBS encryption by default is enabled in the region
controls.rationale: Default encryption ensures new volumes and snapshot copies are encrypted without per-volume action.
controls.remediation: Enable EBS encryption by default in each in-use region.

controls.title: EBS volumes are encrypted
controls.rationale: The Encrypted attribute shows configured encryption; it does not verify key policy, grants or key rotation.
controls.remediation: Create an encrypted snapshot copy, restore it to a new encrypted volume and replace the unencrypted volume.

controls.title: Root account has MFA enabled
controls.benchmark_theme: Identity and Access Management: root account protection
controls.rationale: The root user has unrestricted access and cannot be limited by IAM policy; MFA is the primary compensating control.
controls.remediation: Sign in as root, register a hardware or virtual MFA device under Security credentials, and store recovery material offline. Prefer a hardware or passkey MFA for root.

controls.title: Root account has no active access keys
controls.benchmark_theme: Identity and Access Management: root account protection
controls.rationale: Root access keys grant unrestricted programmatic access and are rarely required.
controls.remediation: Sign in as root and delete the root access keys; use IAM roles or IAM Identity Center for programmatic access.

controls.title: IAM users with console access have MFA
controls.benchmark_theme: Identity and Access Management: multi-factor authentication
controls.rationale: Passwords alone are vulnerable to phishing and credential stuffing.
evidence_requirements: Credential report columns password_enabled and mfa_active per user
controls.remediation: Enrol each console user in MFA, or remove console access and federate through IAM Identity Center.

controls.title: Credentials unused beyond the configured threshold are disabled
controls.benchmark_theme: Identity and Access Management: credential hygiene
controls.rationale: Unused passwords and access keys widen the attack surface without delivering value.
evidence_requirements: Credential report last-used and creation/rotation dates for passwords and access keys
controls.remediation: Deactivate then delete credentials unused for the configured number of days (default 45) after confirming with the owner.

controls.title: Active access keys are rotated within the configured age
controls.benchmark_theme: Identity and Access Management: credential hygiene
controls.rationale: Long-lived access keys increase exposure time after an undetected leak.
evidence_requirements: Credential report access_key_N_last_rotated for active keys
controls.remediation: Create a replacement key, migrate workloads, then deactivate and delete the old key; prefer roles over long-lived keys.

controls.title: No attached customer-managed policy grants full administrative access
controls.benchmark_theme: Identity and Access Management: least privilege
controls.rationale: Policies allowing all actions on all resources defeat least privilege and magnify the impact of any credential compromise.
evidence_requirements: Policy document statements (effect, actions, resources, condition presence) of attached customer-managed policies
controls.remediation: Replace the policy with scoped permissions (use IAM Access Analyzer policy generation) and detach the administrative policy from principals that do not need it.

controls.title: IAM password policy meets the configured baseline
controls.benchmark_theme: Identity and Access Management: password policy
controls.rationale: A weak or absent account password policy permits guessable IAM user passwords.
controls.remediation: Set a password policy with the configured minimum length (default 14) and reuse prevention (default 24), or eliminate IAM user passwords via federation.

controls.title: IAM Access Analyzer is active in the region
controls.benchmark_theme: Identity and Access Management: external access analysis
controls.rationale: Access Analyzer identifies resources shared outside the account or organization.
evidence_requirements: accessanalyzer:ListAnalyzers entries with status ACTIVE and type ACCOUNT or ORGANIZATION
controls.remediation: Create an account or organization analyzer in each in-use region.

controls.title: No attached customer-managed policy uses broad service wildcards or Allow with NotAction
controls.benchmark_theme: Identity and Access Management: least privilege
controls.rationale: Service-wide wildcards on all resources, and Allow combined with NotAction, grant far more than is usually intended.
evidence_requirements: Policy document statements of attached customer-managed policies
controls.remediation: Enumerate the specific actions and resource ARNs required and replace wildcard or NotAction grants.

controls.title: AdministratorAccess is not attached to IAM users or groups
controls.benchmark_theme: Identity and Access Management: least privilege
controls.rationale: Attaching the AWS-managed AdministratorAccess policy to users or groups grants unrestricted access to long-lived principals; roles with MFA/SSO are the safer pattern. Customer-managed admin policies are covered by IAM-006.
controls.remediation: Detach AdministratorAccess from users and groups; grant administrative access through short-lived, MFA- or SSO-protected roles and scope permissions to what each job needs.

controls.title: A multi-region CloudTrail trail is logging
controls.rationale: Without an active multi-region trail, API activity in unused regions can go unrecorded.
controls.remediation: Create a multi-region trail (or organization trail) and start logging.

controls.title: CloudTrail log file validation is enabled
controls.rationale: Digest files let you detect modification or deletion of delivered log files.
controls.remediation: Enable log file validation on the trail.

controls.title: CloudTrail is logging and delivering to S3 without errors
controls.rationale: A trail that is stopped, has no destination, or reports delivery errors silently loses audit evidence.
controls.remediation: Start logging, correct the bucket policy or KMS permissions named in the delivery error.

controls.title: CloudTrail delivers events to CloudWatch Logs
controls.rationale: CloudWatch Logs integration enables near-real-time metric filters and alarms.
controls.remediation: Configure the trail to send events to a CloudWatch Logs log group.

controls.title: CloudTrail S3 bucket is not publicly accessible
controls.benchmark_theme: Logging and monitoring: CloudTrail log bucket protection
controls.rationale: Public access to audit logs discloses sensitive account activity and permits tampering if write access is exposed.
controls.remediation: Enable all four S3 Block Public Access settings on the bucket and remove public statements from its policy.

controls.title: CloudTrail S3 bucket has server access logging enabled
controls.benchmark_theme: Logging and monitoring: CloudTrail log bucket protection
controls.rationale: Access logs on the audit-log bucket record who read or attempted to change evidence.
controls.remediation: Enable server access logging to a separate, protected logging bucket.

controls.title: CloudWatch log groups retain logs for at least the configured period
controls.rationale: Short retention discards evidence needed for investigations.
controls.remediation: Set the retention policy of each log group to at least the configured number of days (default 365) or export to long-term storage.

controls.title: Unauthorized API call metric filter and alarm exist
controls.benchmark_theme: Logging and monitoring: CloudTrail metric filters and alarms
controls.rationale: Spikes in unauthorized or access-denied calls often indicate reconnaissance or misuse.
controls.remediation: Create a metric filter on the CloudTrail log group for UnauthorizedOperation and AccessDenied* error codes, and an alarm with a notification action.

controls.title: Root account usage metric filter and alarm exist
controls.benchmark_theme: Logging and monitoring: CloudTrail metric filters and alarms
controls.rationale: Any use of the root account is a rare, high-signal event.
controls.remediation: Create a metric filter on userIdentity.type = Root (excluding AwsServiceEvent) and an alarm with a notification action.

controls.title: Console sign-in without MFA metric filter and alarm exist
controls.benchmark_theme: Logging and monitoring: CloudTrail metric filters and alarms
controls.rationale: Console sign-ins without MFA indicate accounts not protected by a second factor.
controls.remediation: Create a metric filter for ConsoleLogin events where MFAUsed is No and an alarm with a notification action.

controls.title: GuardDuty detector is enabled in the region
controls.rationale: GuardDuty provides managed threat detection over CloudTrail, VPC flow and DNS logs.
controls.remediation: Enable GuardDuty in every in-use region, ideally centrally managed through AWS Organizations.

controls.title: AWS Config recorder is recording and delivering in the region
controls.rationale: Configuration history supports change tracking and incident investigation.
controls.remediation: Create a configuration recorder and delivery channel, start the recorder, and fix any delivery failures.

controls.title: Security groups do not allow public ingress to sensitive ports
controls.rationale: Administrative and database ports reachable from the internet are routinely scanned and attacked.
evidence_requirements: ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups IpPermissions with 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 sources and port ranges
controls.remediation: Restrict sources to known CIDRs, security groups or a VPN; use SSM Session Manager instead of SSH or RDP.

controls.title: Default security groups restrict all traffic
controls.rationale: Resources launched without an explicit group fall into the default group; leaving it permissive creates accidental exposure.
evidence_requirements: ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups default group ingress and egress rule counts
controls.remediation: Remove all inbound and outbound rules from the default security group in every VPC and use purpose-built groups.

controls.title: Security groups do not allow public ingress on all ports or protocols
controls.rationale: Allowing all traffic from the internet exposes every listening service on attached resources.
evidence_requirements: ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups rules with protocol -1 or the full port range from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0
controls.remediation: Replace the rule with the specific ports and sources required.

controls.title: Security groups do not allow unrestricted egress on all protocols
controls.rationale: Unrestricted egress eases data exfiltration and command-and-control; it is the AWS default, so this is a hardening signal rather than a defect. Default security groups are covered by NET-002.
evidence_requirements: ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups IpPermissionsEgress with protocol -1 to 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0
controls.remediation: Limit egress to required destinations and ports where the workload allows it.

controls.title: No EBS snapshots owned by the account are public
controls.rationale: A public snapshot lets any AWS account copy its data.
controls.remediation: Make the snapshot private (modify snapshot attribute to remove the all group) and review whether its data was exposed.

controls.title: No AMIs owned by the account are public
controls.rationale: Public AMIs may embed credentials, keys or proprietary software.
controls.remediation: Make the AMI private and rotate any secrets it may contain.

controls.title: RDS DB instances are not publicly accessible
controls.rationale: PubliclyAccessible resolves the endpoint to a public IP; actual reachability also depends on security groups and routing, which this control does not evaluate.
controls.remediation: Modify the instance to disable public accessibility and place it in private subnets.

controls.title: RDS DB instances have storage encryption enabled
controls.rationale: StorageEncrypted shows configured encryption; it does not verify key policy or grants.
controls.remediation: Restore an encrypted copy from a snapshot and cut over; encryption cannot be enabled in place.

controls.title: S3 account-level Block Public Access is fully enabled
controls.rationale: The account-level setting is a guardrail that overrides bucket-level misconfiguration.
controls.remediation: Enable all four account-level Block Public Access settings.

controls.title: S3 bucket Block Public Access is effectively enabled
controls.rationale: Block Public Access prevents ACLs and policies from making data public. Effective protection combines account and bucket settings.
controls.remediation: Enable all four Block Public Access settings on the bucket or at account level.

controls.title: S3 bucket policy does not make the bucket public
controls.rationale: S3's own policy-status evaluation reports whether the bucket policy grants public access.
controls.remediation: Remove wildcard principals from the bucket policy or constrain them with conditions such as aws:SourceVpce or aws:PrincipalOrgID.

controls.title: S3 bucket has default encryption configured
controls.rationale: Default encryption configuration shows intended at-rest protection. It does not prove that every existing object is encrypted with the expected key, nor that key policies are sound.
evidence_requirements: s3:GetEncryptionConfiguration algorithm and key id presence
controls.remediation: Configure default encryption (SSE-KMS with a customer-managed key where key control is required) and re-encrypt existing objects if needed.

controls.title: S3 bucket has server access logging enabled
controls.rationale: Access logs support investigation of data access.
controls.remediation: Enable server access logging to a dedicated bucket, or rely on CloudTrail data events where appropriate.

controls.title: S3 bucket policy denies non-TLS requests
controls.rationale: Without a deny on aws:SecureTransport=false, clients can use unencrypted HTTP.
evidence_requirements: s3:GetBucketPolicy statements with Deny and aws:SecureTransport false
controls.remediation: Add a bucket policy statement denying all S3 actions when aws:SecureTransport is false.

controls.title: S3 bucket ACL does not grant access to everyone
controls.rationale: ACL grants to the AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers groups expose bucket contents to the internet or to any AWS account, independent of bucket policy.
evidence_requirements: s3:GetBucketAcl grants whose grantee URI is the AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers group
controls.remediation: Remove the group grants from the bucket ACL, enable Object Ownership 'Bucket owner enforced' to disable ACLs, and enable Block Public Access.
